title: Best Dehumidifier for Smoke Smell (2026): What Actually Works
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers and Air Purifiers for Smoke Smell
dek: A dehumidifier won't pull smoke out of the air, but drier air makes a smoky room smell less. Pair it with the right purifier and the odor finally fades.
description: Looking for a dehumidifier for smoke smell? Here’s the honest answer, plus the carbon air purifiers and HEPA dehumidifier combos that actually cut smoke odor.
intro: Let's start with the honest answer: a **dehumidifier for smoke smell** can help, but it can't do the job alone. A dehumidifier removes water vapor. Smoke is a mix of fine particles and gases, and the odor you notice comes mostly from those gases and the sticky residue they leave on walls, fabrics and carpet. Pulling water out of the air doesn't capture any of that.

What lower humidity does do is calm the smell down. Smoke residue and many household odors tend to smell stronger on muggy days, because damp air helps odor molecules release from surfaces. Holding a room at 40–50% takes the edge off — and stops a musty smell from piling on top. The particles and gases themselves are a job for an air purifier with a **True HEPA filter** and **activated carbon**.

So this guide recommends setups, not miracles: the purifiers that do the heavy lifting on smoke odor, a dehumidifier to pair with them, and two combo units that put HEPA filtration and dehumidification in one box for smaller or damper rooms.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers and purifiers for smoke smell

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compared manufacturer specifications — clean air delivery rates, filter types, DOE dehumidifier ratings and room-size claims — checked the CPSC database for recalls, and read owner reviews from people dealing with cigarette smoke, a neighbor's smoke and wildfire seasons.

We favored purifiers that combine True HEPA and activated carbon with honest airflow numbers, and dehumidifiers with set-percentage humidistats. We excluded ozone generators and devices that rely on ozone to mask odors. Every pick is available on Amazon.

sections.heading: What to look for in a smoke odor setup

items.label: Activated carbon, and plenty of it
items.text: Carbon is what absorbs odor gases. Thin carbon-dusted pre-filters fill up fast; thicker carbon layers or smoke-specific filters last longer.

items.label: True HEPA for particles
items.text: Smoke particles are tiny. A True HEPA filter is the standard for catching them.

items.label: Enough airflow
items.text: Choose a purifier whose CADR is at least two-thirds of your room's square footage, more for heavy smoke.

items.label: A humidistat on the dehumidifier
items.text: Hold 40–50%. Our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) explains seasonal targets.

items.label: No ozone
items.text: Skip ozone generators, and check that any ionizer is certified for low ozone output by the California Air Resources Board.

blocks.text: Some smells, yes; smoke, only indirectly. A dehumidifier is the main fix for odors caused by moisture, and a supporting player for everything else. Here's how it breaks down:

Does a dehumidifier help?

blocks.text: If the smell is closer to damp basement than ashtray, you need our [best dehumidifier for musty smell](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-musty-smell/) guide instead. For a deeper look at which machine does what, see [air purifier vs. dehumidifier](/guides/dehumidifier-vs-air-purifier/).
Will a dehumidifier help with cat urine smell?

Only after you treat the source. Old urine spots often smell strongest on humid days, because moisture reactivates the residue. An enzyme cleaner breaks down what's causing the odor; a dehumidifier holding 40–50% then keeps any remaining trace from flaring up when the weather turns muggy.

sections.heading: How to get rid of smoke smell in a room

blocks.text: Machines keep a clean room fresh; they can't clean it for you. Work through these steps in order:

items: **Stop the source.** If someone smokes indoors, no setup will keep up. Move it outside and close the door behind it.
**Wash what you can.** Curtains, bedding, throw pillows and clothes hold a surprising share of the smell.
**Clean hard surfaces.** Wash walls, ceilings, cabinets and windows; smoke film is often visible as a yellow tint on cloths.
**Replace the HVAC filter,** and consider professional duct cleaning if the whole house smells.
**Seal stubborn walls.** If the smell bleeds through after washing, an odor-blocking primer before repainting locks it in.
**Run the purifier and dehumidifier together** — purifier on auto, dehumidifier at 45% — and keep them going for weeks, not hours.

blocks.title: Skip the ozone generator
blocks.text: The EPA advises against using ozone generators in occupied spaces. Ozone at levels people can safely breathe does little against odors, and higher levels irritate lungs. Restoration pros sometimes use ozone treatments in empty homes; that's a job for them, not a plug-in gadget.

Two machines win in almost every room bigger than a large bedroom. A dedicated purifier moves far more air through far more filter media than a dehumidifier's HEPA stage, and a dedicated dehumidifier removes far more water than a small combo's thermoelectric module. Combos earn their place in small, damp spaces — closets, small bedrooms, studio apartments — where one quiet box is the practical choice. For apartment-sized setups, see our [best dehumidifier for apartment](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-apartment/) picks.

A dehumidifier won't remove smoke, but it makes a smoky room smell better by keeping humidity in check. The best smoke odor setup is a carbon-and-HEPA purifier such as the **Levoit Core 400S** (or the **Core 600S** for open rooms and the **Core 300S** for bedrooms), paired with a dehumidifier like the **Midea Cube 35** if the space runs humid. For a single machine in a damp room, the **AirCyan 32 Pint with HEPA** handles moisture well; for a closet or small bedroom, the **Tenergy Sorbi** is a fair compromise. Clean first, then let the machines keep it that way.

faqs.q: Does a dehumidifier help with smoke smell?
faqs.a: Indirectly. It doesn't capture smoke particles or odor gases, but lowering humidity to 40–50% makes absorbed smoke odors less noticeable and stops musty smells from adding to them. For the smoke itself, use an air purifier with True HEPA and activated carbon.

faqs.q: Do dehumidifiers help with smells in general?
faqs.a: They're the main fix for musty and mildew smells, which come from moisture. For smoke, pet, cooking or chemical odors, a dehumidifier only plays a supporting role; clean the source and use a carbon air purifier.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier help with cat urine smell?
faqs.a: Only after you treat the spot with an enzyme cleaner. Humidity reactivates old urine residue, so a dehumidifier helps keep a treated area from smelling again on muggy days.

faqs.q: What is the best machine for smoke smell?
faqs.a: An air purifier with True HEPA and a substantial activated-carbon filter, sized so its CADR is at least two-thirds of the room's square footage. The Levoit Core 400S suits most living rooms.

faqs.q: Is a dehumidifier and air purifier combo good for smoke?
faqs.a: For small rooms, it's a reasonable compromise. In larger rooms, a separate purifier and dehumidifier each do their job far better than a combo's shared fan and small filters.

faqs.q: Why does my dehumidifier smell like smoke or burning?
faqs.a: A dusty coil or heater element can smell briefly when a unit starts, but a persistent burning smell is a warning sign. Unplug it and check for damage; our [dehumidifier not working](/guides/dehumidifier-not-working/) guide covers next steps.
